The towns are fed through the winter of 1918 and the January strikes do not spread, though the monarchy's other troubles remain. What actually happened: Austro-Hungarian forces occupied parts of Ukraine from February 1918, after the treaty of Brest-Litovsk with the Ukrainian People's Republic, and Odessa was taken by Austro-Hungarian troops in the spring. The grain that came out was far less than had been promised, and the monarchy was hungry in the summer. The Ukrainian grain that the monarchy was promised under the treaty of February 1918 was a small part of what the cities needed, and the hunger of that summer was one of the causes of the strikes and the mutinies that followed.Your commandMajor48 out of 100Ground held: the homeland held, with some losses; 2 places held or taken beyond the record, 2 lost or not taken20/30Power at the close: the three meters together stood at -194/2
